scenes.narration: Mid-career, the AI conversation lands differently than it does for someone just starting out.
You've got a decade of judgment, relationships, and hard-won context — exactly the things AI is worst at replicating.

vars.label: Mid-career, you already have
vars.heading: Exactly What AI Is Worst at Replicating

scenes.narration: So the most useful question about AI and your career isn't "will it replace my job?" It's "how will it change my job. And how do I aim myself at the more valuable part?"

pointCues: how will it change my job

vars.bTitle: How Will It Change My Job?
vars.bSub: And where's the more valuable part

scenes.narration: Mid-career, you have the leverage to do exactly that, because you already understand your role deeply enough to see which parts are shifting.

vars.statement: You Have the Leverage to Do Exactly That

scenes.narration: Here's a practical way to think about your current role and your next move.

vars.statement: A Practical Way to Think About Your Next Move

scenes.narration: First: what tasks might AI do faster or cheaper? Assume those get automated or accelerated, and don't defend them.

vars.heading: What Tasks Might AI Do Faster or Cheaper?
vars.chips: Get automated or accelerated,Don't defend them

scenes.narration: Second: what becomes more valuable as a result? Usually it's the judgment, the relationships, the creativity, and the oversight around those tasks — the very things your experience makes you good at.

vars.label: Second
vars.heading: What Becomes More Valuable as a Result?

scenes.narration: Third: how do you reposition toward that more valuable part? This is where AI-era thinking meets everything else in this course.

vars.heading: How Do You Reposition Toward That?

scenes.narration: Your Next Move Statement, your repositioned resume, and your visibility can all be aimed at the human, high-judgment work that grows more valuable as AI spreads.

vars.kicker: Aim these at the valuable part
vars.statement: Aimed at the Human, High-Judgment Work
vars.lines: Your Next Move Statement|Your repositioned resume|Your visibility

scenes.narration: Take an example. AI can draft a first pass of almost any document, analysis, or plan. That makes the drafting less scarce.

stepCues: ai can draft a first pass
that makes the drafting less scarce

scenes.narration: And it makes the person who knows what's worth saying, who can judge quality, who owns the client relationship, and who can stake their reputation on the call more valuable.

pointCues: and who can stake their reputation

vars.label: That makes someone else more valuable
vars.heading: Who Becomes More Valuable
vars.point4: Can stake their reputation on the call

scenes.narration: Mid-career, that person is you. So aim your next move at that part.

The frame that matters is this: AI is very good at tasks, and your value has always been more than tasks. The skills that stay valuable are the ones that are hardest to automate — the ones that make you the person who can direct AI well, rather than compete with it.

pointCues: your value has always been more than tasks

scenes.narration: So here are the durable, human-centered skills worth investing in. Judgment and decision-making.

vars.context: So here are the durable, human-centered skills worth investing in

scenes.narration: Deciding what's worth doing — and what "good" looks like — is far harder to automate than doing the task itself. Your experience is the raw material here.
Communication and persuasion. Explaining ideas clearly, building trust, and moving people to act. Mid-career, this often becomes your primary value.

vars.heading: Your Primary Value, Mid-Career
vars.chips: Explaining ideas clearly,Building trust,Moving people to act

scenes.narration: Relationships and collaboration. Leadership, empathy, working across teams — deeply human, deeply valued, and exactly what sponsorship and advancement run on.

vars.statement: What Sponsorship and Advancement Run On

scenes.narration: Learning how to learn. In a fast-changing field, the ability to pick up new tools quickly beats mastery of any single tool. Staying curious is a competitive advantage at every level.
And working with AI. Knowing how to prompt it, check it, and combine its outputs with your own judgment is quickly becoming a baseline professional skill — and a visible one you can demonstrate.

None of these asks you to out-compute a machine. They ask you to be a thoughtful, capable professional who uses powerful tools well. And mid-career, you're better positioned to do that than almost anyone.

vars.kicker: None of this is out-computing a machine
vars.statement: A Thoughtful, Capable Professional Who Uses Powerful Tools Well

scenes.narration: So don't just ask what AI replaces. Ask what it changes — and aim yourself at the part that's worth more.
